title: Radioactive decay: types and properties; Particles, antiparticles and classification
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: N02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; N02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; N02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; P01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: N02-1#N.5, P01-1#N.4, N02-1#N.8b, N02-1#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Beta-minus particle
items.clue: A fast electron emitted from the nucleus, charge –e.

items.label: Alpha particle
items.clue: A helium-4 nucleus: 2 protons and 2 neutrons, charge +2e.

items.label: Gamma ray
items.clue: A high-energy photon with no charge and no mass, emitted by a nucleus.

items.label: Antiparticle
items.clue: Counterpart of a given type of matter, with the same mass but the opposite charge.

questions.stem: A nucleus has nucleon number A and proton number Z. It undergoes an alpha decay, and the nucleus formed then undergoes a beta-minus decay. Which expression gives the number of neutrons in the final nucleus?
Enormous numbers of neutrinos produced by nuclear fusion in the Sun pass through Earth every second, and almost none of them are absorbed or deflected on the way. Which statement best explains this?

options.text: They are uncharged, and uncharged particles pass through matter freely.
Their mass is so small that they slip through the gaps between atoms.
They are long-wavelength electromagnetic waves, which pass through solids.
No electric or strong forces act on them; only the weak force and gravity do.

questions.stem: A student proposes that a free neutron decays into a proton and an electron and nothing else: n → p + e⁻. Which conservation law that holds in all nuclear decays would this proposal break?

options.text: Charge, since two charged particles would come from one neutral particle
Nucleon number, since a neutron would be replaced by a proton
Lepton number, since the number of electrons and neutrinos would rise
Mass, since the proton and electron have less mass than the neutron

questions.stem: Thorium-232 (²³²₉₀Th) decays through a chain of α and β⁻ decays to stable lead-208 (²⁰⁸₈₂Pb). How many α decays and how many β⁻ decays are there in the chain?
